problem_markdown: For distinct positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots$, prove $\sum_{k=1}^n a_k/k^2\ge\sum_{k=1}^n1/k$ for every $n\ge1$.
solutions_markdown: Fix $n$ and sort the first $n$ values increasingly as $b_1<\cdots<b_n$. Because the weights $1/k^2$ decrease, exchanging any inverted pair of values cannot increase the weighted sum. Therefore $\sum a_k/k^2\ge\sum b_k/k^2$. Distinct positivity implies $b_k\ge k$, so the latter is at least $\sum k/k^2=\sum1/k$.
